brief: Monthly GS cross-sector desk sentiment survey (TMT, Financials, Healthcare, Consumer, Industrials, Energy, Special Situations), no single thesis. TMT: September's biggest inflection was META's best month since July 2013 on Muse-driven product momentum, plus a trending Inference Economy theme (capex/asset-light AI plays via data infra and cyber). Q3 hyperscaler earnings and cloud margins are next catalysts. Financials: higher rates hit capital markets activity. Bank earnings (10/13) and the October FOMC are next. Healthcare: TMO's long-range-plan walkthrough at a competitor conference was the key inflection. Consumer: sentiment turned more negative on European-exposed apparel names and on low-income consumers given a widening K-shaped economy, per feedback at GS's Retail conference, while cruise bookings strengthened. Core consumer stocks have stayed largely immune to agentic-AI pressure, which instead hit internet names, financials and business services. Industrials: the sector fell to 1- and 5-year lows versus the market as AI/data-center, short-cycle, aerospace and transport sentiment soured. Conference commentary from JBHT, CARR and LECO flags price/cost as a widening Q3 headwind. Energy: refiners screen bullish on 3Q revisions but specialists are cautious on diesel-export-ban risk. Special situations: MGM is reportedly now pursuing PPLI, a day after PPLI dropped its own $48.30-per-share bid for MGM.
